title: The Top 7 HR Challenges in Healthcare (and the Trends Behind Them)
summary: The top HR challenges in healthcare, from staffing shortages and turnover to credential tracking and burnout, plus the trends behind them.
body_markdown:
For HR teams, keeping work moving means more than connecting systems. Routine requests also need timely, consistent answers. For that reason, HR teams desperately need tech that can pull them out of the administrative weeds so they can focus on people. After all, HR teams across hospitals, clinics, long-term care, home health and behavioral health face these top challenges:


1. staffing shortages
2. turnover and retention
3. credential and recertification tracking
4. 24/7 scheduling
5. multirate pay and payroll accuracy
6. data security and HIPAA
7. burnout


Fortunately, technology that both helps HR in healthcare directly overcome these challenges and frees them to better understand these issues already exists. Decisioning logic helps by automatically applying the policies you set to resolve time-off requests, shift swaps, timecard approvals and more, rather than requiring a manual decision for each one.


## What does HR do in healthcare?


In healthcare, HR works to keep qualified people on every shift, paid accurately and supported well enough to stay. That covers hiring, credential tracking, round-the-clock scheduling, complex payroll, training and data protection.


The workload is growing. According to the[U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/home.htm) , overall employment in healthcare occupations is projected to grow much faster than the average for all occupations from 2025 to 2035. The bureau projects 1.9 million openings each year, on average, in these occupations. In most organizations, HR touches each opening several times, from posting the job to verifying credentials and running a first paycheck.


## 1. Staffing shortages


### *Why are healthcare staffing shortages so hard to solve?*


Healthcare staffing shortages are hard to solve because the pressure is heaviest right now, varies widely by state and hits some roles harder than others.


Nursing illustrates the challenge. According to the[Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA)](https://bhw.hrsa.gov/sites/default/files/bureau-health-workforce/data-research/nursing-projections-factsheet.pdf) , the projected shortage of registered nurses (RNs) is 8% in 2028 and 3% in 2038. Even that smaller gap represents a shortage of 108,960 full-time equivalent (FTE) RNs.


While the national RN shortage is projected to ease, that doesn’t mean staffing will become easy, considering these three factors:


- **The projected pressure is front-loaded.** The largest gap in HRSA’s projections is sooner, so today’s hiring teams face the tightest market.
- **Shortages are local.** HRSA notes that projected supply adequacy of RNs varies considerably across states, ranging from a shortage of 22% in California to a projected 79% oversupply in Wyoming in 2038. A healthy national average doesn’t help a unit in a short-supply state.
- **Some roles aren’t improving.** HRSA projects licensed practical nurse (LPN) supply will meet 70% of demand in 2038, and specialty units can’t always backfill with any available nurse.


### *How HR can close staffing gaps faster*


Start with speed. Each manual handoff adds another step between application and offer. Handling job posts, candidate messages, offers and new-hire paperwork in one database can shorten that wait.


Dominion Care, a healthcare provider, saw the difference when it switched back to Paycom. A[healthcare HR technology case study](https://www.paycom.com/blog/resources-content/health-care-hr-technology-case-study/) shows how Paycom helped the organization cut the steps needed for recruitment by 50% and hire 81 employees in four months. As its talent acquisition manager put it: “With our previous provider, it would take a candidate from moment of application to offer about 15 steps. Now, with Paycom, that is done within an average of seven.”


Then build depth with cross-training. When a behavioral health unit or long-term care wing runs short, staff trained in more than one area can help cover the gap. A[learning management system](https://www.paycom.com/software/paycom-learning/) (LMS) helps when it lets you:


- **curate content for your field** , such as healthcare, behavioral health, home health and long-term care, and CNA course collections
- **assign courses automatically** by role, department or work location
- **follow up on enrollment** with automatic reminders to employees and their managers until training is complete


Paycom Learning does all three. Cross-training also doubles as a growth path, an area many employers haven’t built yet. Gallagher’s Workforce Trends Report Series 2024 Healthcare Addendum found that only 43% of healthcare organizations support employees in developing and pursuing a career.


## 2. Turnover and retention


### *What’s driving turnover in healthcare?*


Nationally, the acute care hospital turnover rate is 18.5%, and staff RN turnover is recorded at 17.6%, according to NSI Nursing Solutions’ annual[National Health Care Retention & RN Staffing Report](https://www.nsinursingsolutions.com/Documents/Library/NSI_National_Health_Care_Retention_Report.pdf) .


Many of the reasons people leave are operational, not just financial:


- **schedules they can’t plan around** , such as last-minute shift changes or time-off requests that sit unanswered
- **inconsistent decisions** , where approval depends on which manager is working
- **no visible path forward** , especially for early-career nurses and allied health staff


### *How decisioning logic helps with scheduling and time off*


Employees want fast, fair answers about their time, and decisioning logic is designed to deliver both. With Paycom’s Time-Off Requests featuring GONE®, organizations set the rules once, and requests are automatically approved, denied or held based on criteria like accruals, company policy and compliance requirements. The same policy applies whether a request comes in on a Tuesday afternoon or a Saturday night.


Shift-swap approvals in Paycom’s Scheduling tool can follow the rules you set, too. In a healthcare organization with round-the-clock coverage, a shift exchange isn’t just a convenience for an employee; it’s a change to the team’s schedule. Paycom’s Scheduling tool lets shift-swap approvals follow preconfigured rules, giving employees flexibility within an organization’s policies. For nurse managers, that means a more consistent approval process instead of handling each exchange differently depending on who’s working.


## 3. Credential and recertification tracking


### *Why is credential tracking such a heavy lift?*


One expired license can take an employee off the schedule and create liability. And most clinical roles carry several credentials, each renewing on its own timeline, and can include:


- an RN license
- a Basic Life Support (BLS) card
- an Advanced Cardiovascular Life Support (ACLS) certification


Multiply that across a few hundred employees, and the expiration dates and renewal deadlines add up quickly.


Keeping credentials current also means making sure employees have access to relevant training. In a Paycom survey of 1,000 U.S. full-time employees, just 26% said their organization offers industry-specific training and certifications.


### *How HR can keep credentials audit-ready*


Keep credentials in the same system as your employee records. Look for[certification-tracking tools](https://www.paycom.com/software/certification-management/) that let employees upload certifications from their phones, route them to an approver and send reminders before anything expires. Because credentials live in the same connected system as scheduling, rules can also block uncredentialed employees from being scheduled or taking a shift swap, creating another way to stay in compliance and protect patients.


## 4. 24/7 scheduling


Having 24/7 scheduling doesn’t mean anyone works around the clock. It means your schedule has to cover every hour of every day, including nights, weekends, holidays and callouts, while giving each employee a predictable, sustainable shift pattern.


### *Why is healthcare scheduling so complex?*


Scheduling in healthcare demands balancing full-time, part-time, per diem, contract and travel staff, each with different availability and credentials, often with thin staffing. Soliant Health’s 2024 State of Healthcare Report uncovers that more than a quarter of healthcare professionals (26%) said “working with a limited staff or a shortage of workers” was the most common issue they faced. Shift swaps add another layer: Each exchange needs to be checked against the employee’s resulting schedule, including any applicable limits on consecutive shifts and required rest between them.


### *How to simplify 24/7 scheduling*


Start with templates for recurring shift patterns. Then look for[scheduling software](https://www.paycom.com/software/scheduling/) that shows the whole schedule at a glance, handles shift exchanges with preconfigured rules and lets employees claim open shifts from their phones. Paycom’s Scheduling tool automatically approves shift swaps that meet preset criteria and supports scheduling requirements such as time between shifts, helping offer flexibility within established rules. Scheduling rules can also keep anyone from being scheduled for, or picking up, a shift (including through a shift swap) unless they hold the required credentials, so coverage stays compliant and patients stay safe.


## 5. Multirate pay and payroll accuracy


Healthcare payroll is rarely one rate times hours worked. It’s often base pay plus shift differentials, overtime, on-call and charge pay, sometimes for the same employee in the same week.


### *Why does healthcare payroll break so easily?*


Every rate change and system handoff creates room for error: an RN who floats between two units at two rates, or a night shift that crosses into a weekend differential. Those factors alone create the potential for costly, time-consuming administrative work and errors. A 2026 EY analysis commissioned by Paycom estimates that **a single payroll error costs a business $339 on average** , a figure that reflects more than the time spent correcting it. The figure is an inflation-adjusted update based on survey research originally conducted in 2022.


### *How to improve payroll accuracy in healthcare*


Reduce payroll errors before they happen by keeping time, scheduling and payroll in one database and using decisioning logic to automatically resolve routine approvals before they reach payroll.


Then ensure employees have a way to access, review, troubleshoot, verify and approve their own paychecks before payroll runs. Beti®, Paycom’s automated payroll experience, identifies errors and guides employees to fix them *before* submission. In its 2023 report,[Nucleus Research](https://www.paycom.com/resources/nucleus-research-beti-bolsters-payroll-success/) found that Beti led to 100% user adoption, reduced payroll corrections by 80%-100% and reduced payroll processing time by 90%.


## 6. Data security and HIPAA


Healthcare compliance extends beyond data security. HR teams also need to verify applicable professional licensure and renewal requirements, such as those set by[state nursing boards](https://www.ncsbn.org/nursing-regulation/licensure.page) , and follow[federal and state labor laws](https://beta.dol.gov/policy-regulations/pay-benefits/wages-hours/compliance-assistance/toolkits/flsa) for minimum wage, overtime and recordkeeping. Review requirements for each role and work location with your compliance or legal team.


Healthcare organizations manage highly sensitive patient and employee information, which makes them attractive targets. According to[IBM’s Cost of a Data Breach Report 2026](https://www.ibm.com/reports/data-breach) , healthcare data breaches cost an average of $6.64 million, making healthcare the costliest industry for data breaches for the 13th consecutive year.


### *How to protect employee data*


Reduce the number of places sensitive data lives. Multiple logins and paper files widen your exposure, while a single-database software with role-based access leaves fewer systems to secure. Ask vendors for independent certifications and audits, not just assurances.


Paycom is ISO- and SOC-certified, and it is recognized by the American Hospital Association as its preferred payroll provider for cybersecurity. Paycom also owns and operates its data centers and is one of only five companies in the U.S. with Tier IV certification for facility construction — the Uptime Institute’s highest level for fault tolerance. Learn more about Paycom’s HR data security standards[here](https://www.paycom.com/about/security/) .


## 7. Burnout


Burnout feeds many of the challenges above.[Gallagher’s Workforce Trends Report Series 2024](https://www.ajg.com/-/media/files/gallagher/us/news-and-insights/2024/2024-wtrs_healthcare-addendum.pdf) Healthcare Addendum finds that 81% of surveyed healthcare employers agree leaders are concerned about the impact of stress and burnout on their organization.


### *How HR can reduce burnout*


HR can’t remove the emotional weight of patient care, but it can take administrative work off the people closest to patients. That’s the third place decisioning logic helps: When routine approvals for time off, shift swaps and timecards follow rules you’ve already set, nurse managers spend less time approving requests after a long shift and more time supporting their teams.


A commissioned study conducted by Forrester Consulting on behalf of Paycom revealed how automating time-off tasks benefited a composite organization based on interviewed clients over a projected three-year period.* According to the study, the composite organization annually saved each manager nearly a workweek† of unproductive hours; HR, finance and admin staff nearly 200 hours; and up to 240 hours in avoidable overtime.


## HR trends in the healthcare industry


HR trends in the healthcare industry include prioritizing retention, building career paths, addressing burnout, automating routine administrative work and consolidating HR technology.


- **Retention over recruitment.** Keeping experienced employees is a priority alongside filling vacancies. According to NSI Nursing Solutions’[National Health Care Retention & RN Staffing Report](https://www.nsinursingsolutions.com/Documents/Library/NSI_National_Health_Care_Retention_Report.pdf) , the acute care hospital turnover rate is 18.5%. For HR, the practical focus is on the everyday retention factors: predictable schedules, consistent decisions and support from managers.
- **Career development and internal mobility.** Building skills gives employees a path forward while helping teams prepare for staffing gaps. According to Gallagher’s Workforce Trends Report Series 2024 Healthcare Addendum, **only 43% of surveyed healthcare organizations support employees in developing and pursuing a career path.**


Start with visible role pathways and training tied to the qualifications each next step requires.


- **Burnout prevention through better work design.** Employee well-being needs attention in scheduling and workload decisions, not just wellness messaging. Gallagher found 81% of healthcare employers agree their leaders are concerned about the impact of stress and burnout on the organization. HR can start by reviewing unpredictable schedules and avoidable administrative work with clinical leaders.
- **Automation with guardrails.** Routine administrative tasks are a practical place to apply policy-based automation while keeping people responsible for exceptions. An October 2025 EY study commissioned by Paycom estimated that manually reviewing or approving a time-off request costs an organization $12.15 on average.†† This cross-industry estimate covers manual processes without a fully automated self-service HCM solution; PTO balance calculation is a separate task. For healthcare teams, the opportunity is to reduce repeated reviews without treating automation as a substitute for clinical or legal judgment.
- **Consolidating HR technology.** Simplifying the technology stack can help teams address fragmented workflows. A commissioned study conducted by Forrester Consulting on behalf of Paycom in May 2025 found that HR personnel and payroll professionals use an average of 6.17 HCM providers.¶ That cross-industry finding gives healthcare HR teams a useful question to ask: Where do hiring, credentials, scheduling and payroll still depend on duplicate entry or manual handoffs?


## Healthcare HR checklist: Is your tech part of the problem?


If you see more than a couple of these warning signs, it may be time to rethink your tools.


**Challenge** **Warning sign** **What to look for**


**Staffing shortages** Candidates wait days for next steps Hiring, offers and onboarding in one workflow


**Specialty gaps** Only a few staff members can cover specialty units LMS with curated content, auto-assignment and reminders


**Turnover** Time-off requests wait on manager approval Rules-based decisioning for time off and shift swaps


**Credentials** Expiration dates live in a spreadsheet Mobile uploads, approver routing and expiry reminders


**24/7 scheduling** Shift swaps happen by text message Templates, shift exchanges and open-shift claiming


**Payroll accuracy** Time data is reentered into payroll One database plus employee pay review before submission


**Data security** Employees juggle multiple HR logins Single database, role-based access and audited certifications


The fewer systems your people have to touch, the more time they can spend with patients.


## HR challenges in healthcare: FAQ


### *What are the biggest HR challenges in healthcare?*


The biggest HR challenges in healthcare are staffing shortages, turnover, credential tracking, 24/7 scheduling, multirate payroll accuracy, data security and burnout.


### *Why is turnover so high in healthcare?*


Turnover is driven by demanding work, staffing shortages, burnout, unpredictable schedules and limited growth paths. Nationally, the acute care hospital turnover rate is 18.5%, and staff RN turnover is recorded at 17.6%, according to NSI Nursing Solutions’ National Health Care Retention & RN Staffing Report.


### *What are the current HR trends in healthcare?*


Current HR trends in healthcare include a shift from recruitment to retention, the automation of routine admin work with people still in charge of key decisions and the consolidation of HR technology.


### *What is decisioning logic in HR?*


Decisioning logic is software that applies your policies automatically. You set rules once, and routine decisions like time-off requests, shift swaps, timecard approvals and more are made automatically and consistently, so employees get faster answers and managers get time back.
